title: Two casks maturing
subtitle: CMWS private casks · Purchased together in 2019
details: Two casks maturing at the distillery
Small sherry firkin — target bottling date: 4 February 2027

storyBlocks.title: A connection to whisky’s beginnings
storyBlocks.text: Our two casks are maturing at Lindores Abbey, a place with a remarkable connection to whisky’s beginnings. In 1494, Friar John Cor, a monk at Lindores, was commissioned to make aqua vitae from malt—the earliest written reference to Scotch whisky production.
storyBlocks.imageAlt: Stone exterior and entrance of Lindores Abbey Distillery

storyBlocks.title: Lot of sevens
storyBlocks.text:
We’re aiming to bottle our small firkin in ’27 at the age of 7 years, 7 months and 7 days. When we suggested this rather unusual bottling date, Lindores Abbey team immediately agreed to play along.

A little patience, and rather a lot of sevens!

storyBlocks.title: Selecting together at Whisky Life Prague
storyBlocks.text: At short notice, Ardnamurchan kindly arranged for cask samples to be brought to Whisky Life Prague 2025, where Antonia Bruce personally led the selection with around 30 CMWS members — far more than could have joined us at the distillery!

storyBlocks.imageCaption: Samples tasted with Antonia Bruce at Whisky Life Prague on 15 November 2025. Guess which one won!?

storyBlocks.title: The finished bottling
storyBlocks.imageAlt: Two CMWS Ardnamurchan cask #2110 bottles showing the narrow side window and front label
storyBlocks.imageCaption: Ardnamurchan’s distinctive bottle includes a narrow side window, making it easy to see how much whisky remains.

storyBlocks.title: A familiar connection
storyBlocks.text:
The same year we selected our Ardnamurchan cask, Independent Spirits: Another Whisky Film (2025) was released. In the film, Alex Bruce reflects on taking Adelphi whisky to new markets and meeting enthusiasts keen to become part of its Scottish story.

His example caught our attention: “Czechoslovakia”, placed rather cheerfully on “the opposite side of the world”. An old country name and a little geographical licence — but a familiar enthusiasm for Scottish whisky. Exactly what CMWS enjoys: bringing people together around a shared connection to Scotch whisky.

storyBlocks.title: Selected at Glenfarclas
storyBlocks.text:
On 30 May 2023, the Glenfarclas team kindly hosted us at the distillery, offering casks from their prestigious The Family Casks programme in our preferred age range.

We selected cask #2993 from Warehouse No. 1 for our CMWS community.

storyBlocks.title: Choosing the presentation
storyBlocks.text: Glenfarclas offered us two packaging options: the traditional wooden Family Casks box and the new black presentation box. We chose the black version for our CMWS bottling.

title: 30 L cask #19/109
subtitle: Official CMWS bottling
note:
Along with the bottles from our two 2019 Raasay casks, the distillery also sent us the actual casks themselves — something that does not normally happen, as distilleries usually retain the empty casks.

Despite the complications of Brexit, Raasay found a practical way to help its EU customers: the distillery shipped all its 30-litre casks destined for the EU together to Berlin, where a local agent forwarded them to their individual owners. A thoughtful arrangement that saved us considerable shipping costs!
imageAlt: CMWS Raasay casks #109 and #110 with Isle of Raasay bottles arranged on top
imageCaption: CMWS Raasay casks #109 and #110, together with the bottles — and, unusually, the original casks themselves.

title: Verdejo · Vintage 2000
subtitle: 21 Year Old · Cask #32940
note:
Our first official bottling to carry the CMWS name and logo.

Covid prevented us from visiting Tomatin, so the distillery kindly sent us samples to select from. After choosing the Verdejo cask in autumn 2020, Tomatin agreed to let it mature to 21 years — and even accommodated our unusual request to bottle it on 12 April 2021, exactly 60 years after Yuri Gagarin became the first man in space.

Distilled in the last century, matured for 21 years, and bottled on a historic anniversary — this whisky was aiming for the stars!
imageAlt: Front label for CMWS Tomatin single cask #32940, bottled in 2021
imageCaption: Front label for CMWS Tomatin #32940 — bottle 1 of 272.

title: Viking Soul #500174
subtitle: 14 Year Old · Firkin European Oak
details: Cask type / finish: Firkin European Oak
note:
Whenever a new private cask arrives, we introduce it to our group in a tasting alongside other expressions from the same distillery. It helps us understand where our cask sits within the distillery’s wider style.

For this tasting, the line-up was unusual: three of the five whiskies were our own Highland Park Viking Soul Cask bottlings — «Òran Na Boii» I, II and III — with two additional rare Highland Park expressions for comparison.
imageAlt: Five Highland Park expressions lined up for a CMWS tasting: «Òran Na Boii» I, II and III, Hobbister and Ingvar
imageCaption: The three «Òran Na Boii» private-cask bottlings tasted alongside Highland Park Hobbister and Ingvar.

storyBlocks.text:
With two successful entries in the second wave of Highland Park’s Viking Soul Cask programme, we had the opportunity to purchase two casks. Highland Park was even happy to offer us two different types — one American oak and one European oak — giving us two quite different whiskies to explore.

By keeping the same name across both waves, we completed our unique trilogy of Highland Park Viking Soul Cask bottlings: «Òran Na Boii» I, II and III.

title: Viking Soul #500153
subtitle: 14 Year Old · Firkin American Oak
details: Cask type / finish: Firkin American Oak
note:
In the second wave of Highland Park’s Viking Soul Cask programme, we encouraged our members to enter the lottery for the right to purchase a cask — and two of them won!

When we informed Highland Park that we would be purchasing two casks, we weren't quite sure what reaction to expect. To our delight, they were genuinely enthusiastic: two winners from the same whisky community!

storyBlocks.text:
A collaborative bottling through Highland Park’s Viking Soul Cask programme became the foundation of our group. The name CMWS had not yet been coined, so we used «Òran Na Boii», meaning Bohemian Rhapsody in Gaelic.

We still appreciate Highland Park’s willingness to approve our unconventional label name!
